title: Charles S. Peirce, the logic papers of 1867 (Proceedings of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences VII) and the six Illustrations of the Logic of Science (Popular Science Monthly XII–XIII, 1877–1878)
edition: The three volumes as printed; the Internet Archive's text layers, held whole, with Peirce's papers located by line

normalization: The Internet Archive's own text layer (_djvu.txt) as served, under original/<identifier>/, copied to text/<slug>.ocr.txt with line endings normalized. The scan is held by reference at its Archive URL and not copied. No text was corrected by hand; the loci keep the OCR's readings. The volumes are held whole because the text layers drop the running heads and the papers' ends cannot be cut by code without guessing; each paper is located by the line of its heading.
scope: The ten papers in which Peirce reclassifies inference as deduction, induction and hypothesis.
why_seated: The third kind of inference named: the beans of the sixth paper (Rule, Case, Result) against the syllogism's one order.

research.study: Critique of Pure Inference (working draft v1.1) and The Production of Readers (#1767), §11.6 "the witnesses between"
research.for: the reception history of inference from the Peripatos to the machine: the commentators who name Aristotle's ἑταῖροι, the Latin handbooks, the early-modern refusals of the syllogism, the nineteenth-century rebuilds, and the traditions that reasoned about inference without the Organon
